main_text.l: Objectum, circa quod omnis de Jure quæ-
stio versatur, aut in Personis est, aut in Rebus
aut in Factis, vide lib.13. Bibliothecæ selectæ
Medium præter generalia hic est duplex:
Libri Juris sunt vel authentici, vel non.
In authenticis excellit Jus Romanum, quo
multi populi utuntur. Cl. Pacius in suâ Isagoge.
Non-authentici sunt varii, de quibus Possevinus
d.l. De jure Romano hic pauca dicere neces-
se habeo, ex Isagoge Pacii, Alberici Gentilis disp-
utationibus de libris Juris Canonici & Civi-
lis, & Antonii Possevini l.13 biblioth. selectæ.

page.notes: Marginal notes as printed, in order: "Objectum" / "Jurispru-dentiæ." (right, beside first paragraph); "Partitio li-brorum Ju-ris." (right, beside the "Libri Juris" line); "Jus civile continetur" / "Institutio-nibus" / "Digestis" / "Codice" / "& Novellis." (right, beside the Jus civile paragraph). The notes in the transcription are merged into the paragraphs where they stand; the note for the Jus civile paragraph is split across its lines in the margin and is recorded here only. The word "Ictorum" is read from a long-J form ("sCtorum") and is given as Ictorum; the first letter of "Justiniano" and "Justiniani" is printed in a long-s-like form and is read as J. "Itaq;" shows a superscript mark that is read as q;.
